description: Naming rules of spec §5, as data for both implementations. Phase 2 pins the title choice: discTitle is the <T> of a movie or series, chapterTitle is the <título cap.> of the file's chapters. original is the TMDB title in the original language (for a chapter, in the series' original language); english is the en-US title. An absent English title is a missing key or an empty string. Sanitizing, folders and file names are added in phase 5. Conservative choices: a title with no letters (digits and signs only) counts as Latin; combining marks are not letters, so a decomposed accent does not make a title non-Latin; a generic title is one of Episode, Episodio, Capítulo, Capitulo or Chapter followed by a number, in any case, whatever the number; the suffix that can be collapsed is ' (N)', ', Part N' or ', Parte N' or a final ' N' (so 'Odisea 2001' and 'Odisea 2002' would share the base 'Odisea'), and the base must not be empty.

discTitle.description: Disc title <T>: the original title when all its letters are Latin, else the English title, else the original title. Empty only when both are empty.

chapterTitle.description: Chapter title <título cap.> of the file's chapters: each chapter takes its original title when that is Latin, else its English title, else nothing (generic titles count as nothing). Several titles are joined with ' + ', except when they all share the same base (the title without a final number, ' (N)' or ', Part N'): then the base is the title. Chapters without title are left out. Empty when no chapter has a title.
